# Prime-power decomposition and original-modulus CRT fibre density

For every positive modulus and natural cutoff Q, split_exists constructs positive factors a,b by strong induction on n, removing one prime at a time, assigning it to the side selected by p <= Q. The smooth and rough predicates require every prime divisor to lie on its respective side. cross_coprime excludes a shared prime. split_unique uses coprime cancellation and divisibility antisymmetry; smooth_power_allocation and rough_power_allocation prove the entire power p^k divides the chosen factor iff it divides the product, for all k. Both predicates survive multiplication, taking divisors and finite LCM. For every finite indexed family (including empty families, repeated moduli and modulus one), family_split produces a,b, proves coprimality of M=lcm(a_i) and B=lcm(b_i), and lcm(n_i)=M*B. Positive LCM follows from positive factors. family_density transports congruence avoidance from a_i*b_i to the original n_i and applies the earlier protected CRT count identity: the density on M*B is the average over h modulo M of fibre avoidance density on B. Thus the prime decomposition is no longer an assumed hypothesis of the arithmetic CRT bridge.

The width theorem is relative to the specified premise partition and semantic binary calculus; changing that proof model is not covered.
